title: Invite a classmate to study
promptText: Write an email inviting a classmate to study with you this weekend. Say what subject you want to study, where and when to meet, and what your classmate should bring.

title: Describe your neighborhood
promptText: Describe the neighborhood where you live or a neighborhood you know well. Explain what places are nearby, what people usually do there, and one thing you like about it.

title: The bus left without me
promptText: Write a short story about a day when someone missed a bus. Show where the person was going, why they were late, and what they did next.

title: Should students wear uniforms?
promptText: Do you think students should wear school uniforms? Give your opinion and support it with two simple reasons or examples.

title: Ask about a lost item
promptText: You left an important item at a café. Write an email to the café. Describe the item, say when and where you left it, and explain how the staff can contact you.

title: A meal I enjoy
promptText: Describe a meal you enjoy. Say what food is in it, when you usually eat it, who you eat it with, and why it is special to you.

title: Give feedback on an event
promptText: You attended a community event last weekend. Write an email to the organizer describing what worked well, one problem you noticed, and one suggestion for the next event.

title: Homework at the weekend
promptText: Some people think students should not receive homework at weekends. Do you agree or disagree? Explain your view with reasons and an example from school life.

title: An unexpected visitor
promptText: Write a story that begins with the sentence: When I opened the door, I could not believe who was standing there. Include a problem, a decision, and a clear ending.

title: An app that helps me
promptText: Describe an app or digital tool that is useful in your daily life. Explain what it does, how you use it, and one way it could be improved.

title: Change a reservation
promptText: You need to change a hotel reservation because your travel dates have moved. Write an email explaining the situation, giving the new dates, and asking about any extra cost.

title: Make cycling easier
promptText: Should cities spend more money on making cycling easier and safer? State your opinion and discuss how the change could affect at least two groups of people.

title: When remote work works
promptText: Companies should allow employees to choose where they work whenever their job can be done remotely. Discuss the strengths and limitations of this idea, then give your position.

title: Resolve a membership problem
promptText: A fitness club continued charging you after you cancelled your membership. Write a formal email that explains the timeline, identifies the resolution you expect, and requests a prompt response.

title: The choice I reconsidered
promptText: Write a story about a character who is certain about an important decision but changes their mind after one conversation. Use details to make the change believable rather than stating it directly.

title: A public space that succeeds
promptText: Describe a public space that brings different people together. Explain how its layout, atmosphere, and rules influence the way people behave there.

title: News through social media
promptText: For many people, social media is now the main way to discover news. Is this change mostly beneficial or mostly harmful? Develop a balanced argument and reach a clear conclusion.

title: Propose a language exchange
promptText: Write an email to a community center proposing a weekly language-exchange program. Explain the need, outline how sessions would work, and address one likely concern.

title: The price of safer streets
promptText: Cities increasingly use cameras and automated systems to improve public safety. Argue where the boundary between collective security and personal privacy should lie, acknowledging a serious objection to your view.

title: A difficult professional choice
promptText: Describe a workplace ethical dilemma in which every available choice has a meaningful cost. Explain the competing responsibilities and the principles someone should use to decide.

title: Challenge a proposed policy
promptText: Your organization plans to monitor all employee messages to prevent data leaks. Write a formal response to leadership that recognizes the risk, challenges the proposal, and offers a proportionate alternative.

title: A memory that shifts
promptText: Write a story in which the narrator retells an important memory but gradually reveals that their version may be incomplete. Use contradictions and selective detail without explicitly calling the narrator unreliable.

title: Who should hold cultural objects?
promptText: When cultural objects were acquired under unequal historical conditions, should museums be required to return them? Develop criteria that could guide difficult cases rather than arguing from one example alone.

title: When professional identity changes
promptText: Describe how a person's professional identity can change after a major success, failure, or career transition. Analyze the tension between external recognition and private values.

material.title: Residential wastewater reuse

stages.label: Collect
stages.description: Wastewater from sinks, showers, and washing machines enters a separate pipe network.

stages.label: Screen
stages.description: A screen removes large solid material from the collected water.

stages.label: Biological treatment
stages.description: Microorganisms break down dissolved organic matter in an aerated tank.

stages.label: Filter
stages.description: The treated water passes through sand and carbon filters.

stages.label: Disinfect
stages.description: Ultraviolet light destroys remaining harmful microorganisms.

stages.label: Redistribute
stages.description: A second pipe network supplies the water to gardens and toilet tanks, after which it can re-enter the system.

keyFeatures: The system forms a cycle rather than a single-use linear process.
Mechanical, biological, and disinfection stages occur before redistribution.

material.title: Producing woollen fabric

stages.label: Shear
stages.description: Fleece is cut from the sheep in a single piece.

stages.label: Sort
stages.description: The fleece is graded by fibre length and any coarse wool is set aside.

stages.label: Scour
stages.description: Sorted wool is washed in warm water to remove grease and dirt.

stages.label: Card
stages.description: Clean fibres are combed until they lie in the same direction.

stages.label: Spin
stages.description: The combed fibres are drawn out and twisted into yarn.

stages.label: Weave
stages.description: Yarn is woven on a loom to form lengths of cloth.

stages.label: Finish
stages.description: The cloth is washed, dyed and pressed before dispatch.

keyFeatures: The process is linear and has seven stages.
Cleaning and alignment both precede any twisting or weaving.

material.title: Approving a new medicine

stages.label: Laboratory
stages.description: A candidate compound is tested on cells and tissue outside the body.

stages.label: Animal study
stages.description: The compound is tested on animals to check safety and dose.

stages.label: Small trial
stages.description: A small group of healthy volunteers receives the compound under supervision.

stages.label: Large trial
stages.description: Hundreds of patients receive either the compound or an existing treatment.

stages.label: Review
stages.description: A regulator examines the trial evidence and decides whether to approve.
